beats.narration_text: Hey Claude — I just read Tanaka's final brand portfolio for INFO 7375. MentionMap, also branded as BrandPulse — an AI tool that turns pasted brand mentions into a morning brief with mood scores, brand archetypes, and draft responses. What does the work tell us?

props.command: I just read Tanaka's final brand portfolio. MentionMap / BrandPulse — AI brand intelligence morning brief for solo founders and growth marketers. What does the work tell us?

beats.role_note: The brief — what was required and what was submitted.
beats.narration_text: Path B required a complete brand system for an AI tool startup. Tanaka submitted 14 slides plus a deployed tool on Hugging Face, a live website, a LinkedIn presence with documented post impressions, and a Substack newsletter. All five Path B elements are present and the tool is live in production.

props.heading: The Brief vs. The Delivery
props.body: All five Path B elements present. Tool live on Hugging Face. Website deployed. LinkedIn post reached 37,706 impressions. Substack launched August 2026.

beats.role_note: Strength 1 — The tool is live and does what the brand claims.
beats.narration_text: The deployed tool at the Hugging Face URL takes pasted brand mentions — tweets, reviews, Reddit posts — and returns a mood score, a brand archetype from twelve options, and platform-specific draft responses. That's the brand promise in action. The fact that it runs at all, publicly, is the work doing what a student-term capstone should do.

beats.role_note: Strength 2 — Competitive positioning identifies the right empty quadrant.
beats.narration_text: The positioning matrix maps easy versus hard on one axis and basic alerts versus deep reports on the other. MentionMap claims the easy-and-deep quadrant that Brandwatch and Sprout Social don't occupy. That's a real insight. Most monitoring tools are either deep and hard or easy and shallow. The quadrant claim is honest.

props.heading: Positioning matrix
props.body: Easy-and-shallow vs. hard-and-deep. MentionMap claims easy-and-deep — the quadrant Brandwatch and Sprout Social do not occupy.

beats.role_note: Gap 1 — The naming is unresolved: MentionMap vs. BrandPulse.
beats.narration_text: The slide deck opens with MentionMap. The tool URL is splitwolf-brandpulse. The roadmap references mentionmap dot vercel dot app. These are three different names for one product in one submission. That's not a minor inconsistency — brand naming is a graded deliverable. The submission needed to commit to one name and use it consistently.

props.heading: Naming Inconsistency
props.body: MentionMap in the deck, BrandPulse in the URL, mentionmap.vercel.app in the roadmap. Three names, one product, one submission. Brand naming is a graded deliverable — this needed to resolve.

beats.role_note: Gap 2 — Brand archetype detection needs a methodology note.
beats.narration_text: The tool claims to identify which of 12 brand archetypes your audience projects onto your brand. That's a substantive claim — brand archetype frameworks have real academic grounding. But the submission doesn't explain how the classification works. Is it a prompt? A classifier? The methodology matters and it's missing.

props.heading: Archetype Claim Without Method
props.body: 12-archetype classification is a substantive claim with real academic backing. The submission doesn't explain how the classification works — prompt, classifier, or rubric. That gap undermines the credibility of the core feature.

beats.role_note: Gap 3 — Business model section has 500 Pro users as a year-2 target with no acquisition path.
beats.narration_text: Five hundred Pro users at 29 dollars equals 174,000 ARR — the math works. But the slide doesn't show how you get from zero to 500. The Product Hunt launch is mentioned in the roadmap. That's an answer to how you generate awareness, not how you convert it. One customer acquisition funnel slide would change this from aspirational to operational.

props.heading: Acquisition gap
props.body: 500 Pro users at $29 = $174K ARR. The math works. The path from zero to 500 does not appear. Product Hunt launch answers awareness, not conversion.

beats.role_note: The roadmap — where the product goes next.
beats.narration_text: The roadmap is concrete: live data connections in August, team dashboard in September, public launch with paid Pro in October, first 100 paying customers by December. That's a real product timeline for a one-semester capstone. Whether it's achievable is a separate question — the fact that specific dates and milestones exist shows product thinking.

props.heading: Roadmap Discipline
props.body: Live data (Aug), team dashboard (Sep), Product Hunt launch + paid Pro (Oct), 100 customers (Dec). Specific dates and milestones exist — that's product thinking, not wishful thinking.

beats.narration_text: Live tool, documented traction, honest competitive positioning, real roadmap. The submission has everything a Path B project should have. The naming inconsistency is the most fixable and most important gap — everything else is a question of depth, and that's expected at this stage.

props.artifactHeading: Live tool, real traction, honest positioning — naming inconsistency is the one fixable blocker.
